chunks: And Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, loves the cooling of a burning liver. Whoever gives water to a burning liver, whether of a beast or otherwise, Allah will shade him in the shade of His Throne on the Day when there is no shade except His shade.

key_terms.الْكَبِدِ الْحَرَّى: the burning liver, meaning intense thirst
key_terms.يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلُّهُ: the Day when there is no shade except His shade

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for giving water to a thirsty animal or person in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the virtue of relieving thirst and showing mercy to living beings. It presents giving water, even to animals, as a deed beloved to Allah, linked to divine reward on the Day of Judgment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1723 - Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:

"Indeed, Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, loves the cooling of a burning liver. Whoever quenches the thirst of a burning liver- whether of an animal or otherwise, Allah (swt) will shade them under the shade of His Throne on the Day when there is no shade except His shade."
